title: PHPStan reads a finally assignment as if it never ran

ground_truth.statement: A `finally` block runs while an exception unwinds towards an outer `catch`, so $cleaned is true when the ternary reads it: the condition is always true and cleaned_flag() always returns 1.

allowed.reason: The finally assignment makes the condition true. A warning that it is always true is correct; a warning that it is always false must still count as a false positive.
A diagnostic correctly identifying the always-true condition is permitted; this case tests false claims about finally, not warning completeness.

notes: PHPStan 2.3.1 reports ternary.alwaysFalse ("Ternary operator condition is always false.") on the ternary, which contradicts the runtime. PHPStan's own rule (src/Rules/Comparison/TernaryOperatorConstantConditionRule.php) reports the constant value of the condition, so alwaysFalse is a semantic claim, not a style preference. Correct always-true diagnostics are allowed. Silence is not a false negative in this case, whose scope is avoiding incorrect claims about finally. Psalm and Mago are silent. The fixture derives from Mago's flow_finally_runs_after_throw.php; runtime/check.php supplies the neutral ground truth.
